decision: For `show PATH --sources` on a single scalar, print the scalar as YAML with its `# from <file>` comment; a text include prints as a literal block with the comment on the header line (option A)
options: (A) Print the scalar as YAML with the comment
(B) Ignore --sources for scalars and print exactly what get prints
(C) Print the plain value, then a separate `# from <file>` line
reason: With --sources the output is always valid YAML and every scalar shows its source, which fits 'the same YAML'. Without --sources a scalar still prints like get. The PO said this case is out of contract and the choice was the agent's.

decision: Write the spec decisions without asking the PO further questions, using the defaults offered in Q1 (layout, literal blocks, comment on header line, relative paths, reconcile first, exit codes, tests move to get)
options: Ask the PO about each choice
Decide and record the defaults unless the PO objects
reason: Only one case was unresolved by the contract and the existing code. The PO replied 'No corrections'.

decision: Print CRLF text includes, and other text a literal block cannot hold, double-quoted with escapes
reason: A literal block can't keep carriage returns. TROUPE-002 requires that data is never altered.

decision: Put exactly one space before `#` in a source comment (the Q1 example had shown two)
`get` does not accept `--sources`; passing it is a usage error (exit 2)
Ask no further questions during planning and record every contract-open choice in research.md as D-1 to D-9
reason: The PO had delegated all contract-open choices as long as they were recorded

decision: Emit the YAML with a custom renderer (`troupe/yamlout.py`) instead of the ruamel dumper
options: ruamel round-trip dumper with comment injection
reason: --sources needs to know which output line holds which scalar, and a dumper does not expose that. Using a dumper would also decide quoting twice, which breaks TROUPE-007. Post-processing lines is fragile for multi-line scalars.

decision: Use one list of lines tagged with their source for both outputs; --sources only appends comments to the tagged lines
reason: The two outputs then differ only by the comments, by construction (US3 scenario 5)

decision: Layout: 2-space indentation, lists indented under their key, compact `- k: v` and `- - a` items, inline `{}`/`[]`, no `---`, a final newline
reason: Common hand-written YAML style; matches the indent step set uses for new collections

decision: Use literal blocks for every text-include value (including one-line or empty text) and for every other string containing a newline; chomping preference is clip, then strip, then keep; use indentation digit 2 when the first line starts with a space
reason: Exact read-back using the same chomping logic as set; multi-line values stay readable

decision: Amend spec FR-008: in YAML output, write float specials as `.inf`/`-.inf`/`.nan` instead of as get prints them
reason: get prints inf/nan, which YAML reads back as strings, so show output would not parse back to the same data
recorded_at: research.md:34-39 (D-3); spec FR-008; questions.md Scored Q3

decision: Quote strings and keys with set's choose_style rules, plus a check that a plain key also round-trips as a key
reason: One quoting rule shared with set (FR-015)

decision: Source label is `os.path.relpath` to the theatre directory with `/` separators, `../` for files outside it, and no special handling for file names containing line breaks
reason: The contract asks for relative paths with `/`; relpath also covers targets outside the theatre. Such file names are vanishingly rare and the contract is silent.

decision: Only flow-scalar lines and literal-block header lines get a comment; collection-opening lines, `{}`/`[]` lines and block body lines get none
reason: These are exactly the lines that hold a scalar; a comment inside a block body would become content

decision: No runtime self-check in show; correctness is proven by parse-back tests
reason: The renderer is pure and deterministic, so a runtime check would only turn a bug into a confusing error

decision: Move the step-1 show scalar tests to test_get.py, switch value-reading helpers to get, and run test_cli_basics' missing-PATH check on get
reason: get is now the value reader; show no longer requires PATH

decision: scalar_of returns `ScalarValue | None` through a frozen wrapper dataclass
reason: None is a valid YAML null, so a bare Optional could not tell a null scalar from a section

decision: Add D-10: write a string plain only if ruamel safe-load reads it back as the same string under both YAML 1.2 and 1.1 (keys must load as exactly {s: 'x'}); otherwise single quotes, else double. The rule is show-only and set's quoting is unchanged.
options: amend NFR-001/D-8 to make YAML 1.2 core the read-back schema
quote anything YAML 1.1/1.2 readers would misread in show (and possibly set)
